start_here_runtime: 57 minutes with the full response; 55–60 with normal variation. The manuscript is 6,722 words at about 120 words per minute.
start_here_cut: If you have 50 minutes: Introduction to 4, Movement 1 to 6, Movement 2 to 6, Movement 3 to 7, Movement 4 to 7, Movement 5 to 7, Application to 5. Keep Judges 5:6–8, the goad, “he also saved Israel,” Matthew 27:42, and Philippians 2:9–11.
start_here_guardrails: Do not pad the story. The brevity is the point; do not invent a backstory, a battle scene, or a romance the text does not give.
Do not glamorize violence or turn Shamgar into a model for private revenge. He is God’s instrument of deliverance from an oppressor.
Be honest about the name. “Son of Anath” is debated; do not settle it beyond the evidence or make it a scandal.
Keep the typology modest. Shamgar is a signpost, not a direct prophecy; the goad is not a prophecy of the nails.
Say plainly that Hebrews 11:32 does not list Shamgar. The omission is about the list, not his salvation.
The gospel must be explicit: the cross, the resurrection, and the name above every name. Do not end on “be faithful” without the Savior.
start_here_evidence: The abandoned highways, the Philistine iron, the oxgoad, and the verdict “he also saved Israel” are doing theological work, and the cross and empty tomb are the turn.

slides.label: 01 · THE BIG IDEA
slides.note: The size of your mention is not the size of your work.

slides.label: 04 · THE FIELD
slides.headline: Six hundred fell.
slides.body: A farmer with an eight-foot pole met a trained column, and the column stopped coming. The text gives a summary, not a battle plan. The point is the disproportion.
slides.footline: One man. One tool. One deliverance.

slides.label: 05 · THE OBJECTION
slides.headline: Is one sentence enough?
slides.quote: “One verse is not enough to build a story on.”
slides.aside1: But the verse ends with the verdict every judge is measured by.
slides.aside2: The record is short. The salvation is real.
slides.footline: The size of your mention is not the size of your work.

slides.label: 06 · THE TOOL
slides.line2: The power of God in his work.
slides.footline: God uses the tool that is already in the hand of the faithful.

slides.label: 07 · THE RECORD
slides.banner_main: “After him was Shamgar the son of Anath, who killed 600 of the Philistines with an oxgoad, and he also saved Israel.”
slides.footline: The canon counts verses. Heaven counts deliverance.

slides.label: 08 · THE GREATER DELIVERER
slides.banner_main: “God has highly exalted him and bestowed on him the name that is above every name.”
lines: Shamgar saved a nation and got one sentence.
Jesus saved the world and was given the Name.
slides.footline: The one-verse deliverer points to the Word made flesh.
